date.noteEn: The Met dates the start to about the fifth century and gives no start year. The range covers that century; the entry places the work under Vakataka patronage, particularly under Harisena (r. c. 460–478).

events.titleEn: Construction and painting of the Ajanta caves begin
events.summaryEn: Cave construction and painting begin at Ajanta in Central India under Vakataka patronage, above all under Harisena. The refined paintings, which the Met calls the earliest examples of painting in India, depict the Buddha, his attendants and scenes from the jataka tales of the Buddha's lives.
events.selectionNote: The entry ranks the Ajanta paintings as the earliest painting in India and names a royal patron. No catalog or English record covers Ajanta.

date.noteEn: The Met dates the westward move to 434. The same entry dates the check in Gaul to 451 and Attila's death to 453; the record's date covers the move only.

events.titleEn: The Huns under Attila move west
events.summaryEn: Under Attila's rule the Huns move west again and defeat many Germanic tribes throughout central Europe. An alliance of Roman and Germanic troops checks Attila's cavalry in Gaul in 451. His death in 453 weakens his empire: the Huns retreat east, and the tribes they had ruled pursue their own territorial ambitions.
events.selectionNote: The catalog records the Hun advance of the 370s (ev-0370-hunnernas-framryckning-vid-donau). This record covers the westward campaign under Attila from 434.

date.noteEn: The Met gives ca. 450 and names no single burial. It presents the urns' depiction of ancestors as an interpretation.

events.titleEn: Royal tombs at Monte Albán hold ceramic funerary urns
events.summaryEn: Royal tombs at Monte Albán contain many large, complex ceramic funerary urns, thought to depict deceased ancestors. Teotihuacan has a neighbourhood for people from Monte Albán, known as the Oaxaca barrio.
events.selectionNote: The catalog dates Monte Albán's rise to c. 500 BC (ev-bc0500-monte-alban-grundas) and its dominance of the valley to c. AD 50 (ev-0050-montealban-dominerar-oaxaca). This record covers the royal tombs of c. AD 450 and the Monte Albán neighbourhood in Teotihuacan.
